mc.prompt: Which event is cytokinesis rather than mitosis?
mc.answer: Separation of cytoplasm into daughter cells
mc.explanation: Cytokinesis divides cytoplasm; mitosis distributes nuclear chromosomes.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: Separation of cytoplasm into daughter cells
Alignment of chromosomes at the equator

writing.prompt: Compare animal and plant cytokinesis and explain how their structures affect the mechanism.
writing.model: Animal cells commonly constrict through a cleavage furrow. Plant cells have a rigid wall, so vesicles establish a cell plate that grows into a partition and new wall. Both separate cytoplasm into daughter cells after nuclear genetic material has been distributed.

checks.title: Meiosis I and separation of homologous chromosomes

mc.prompt: Why is a cell after meiosis I haploid even though its chromosomes remain replicated?
mc.answer: It has one homologue of each chromosome type
mc.explanation: Ploidy counts sets; replication state is a separate property.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: It has one homologue of each chromosome type
It contains only one DNA molecule total

mc.prompt: What makes a tetrad different from one replicated chromosome?
mc.answer: A tetrad contains two replicated homologues and four chromatids
mc.explanation: Pairing two replicated homologues brings four chromatids together.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: A tetrad is always four unreplicated gametes
A tetrad is a single RNA molecule
A tetrad contains two replicated homologues and four chromatids

writing.prompt: Explain how meiosis I reduces chromosome number without separating sister chromatids.
writing.model: Homologous pairs align and the two homologues move to opposite poles during anaphase I. Each future daughter receives one chromosome of each pair, so it is haploid. The sister chromatids within each chromosome remain together until meiosis II.

Explains the causal relationship or calculation, not just the final result.
Uses the stated evidence and avoids a stronger conclusion than it supports.

writing.model: Each cell has n = 4 chromosomes. Each chromosome is still replicated, so there are 8 chromatids per cell. The cell is haploid because it has one homologue of each type, not because the chromatids have separated.

videos.title: Meiosis I and separation of homologous chromosomes — video support
videos.purpose: Trace meiosis I and explain why separation of homologues produces haploid chromosome sets while chromatids remain paired.
videos.fallback: At metaphase I, homologous pairs align at the equator. Their orientation relative to other pairs can vary. A replicated maternal homologue faces one pole and its paternal partner faces the other, but different pairs can orient independently. During anaphase I, the homologues separate. The sister chromatids of each chromosome normally remain joined. The event is therefore different from mitotic anaphase, which separates sister chromatids. After this distribution, each future daughter receives one chromosome of each homologous pair. It has one set rather than two. That is the reduction in ploidy.
